OIML certificates: The OIML certificate number format is typically "R49-1/2006-NL1-13.01" meaning Recommendation R49-1, year 2006, issuing authority NL1, serial 13.01. The register form "R049/2006-NL1-2013.01" is a reformatted canonical form: R049 vs R49 (zero-padding), hyphen vs slash, "2013.01" vs "13.01" (year prefix abbreviation: 13.01 = 2013, certificate 01). Both denote the same certificate, revision 3 in both.

Per the rules: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."

So verdict: same-entity, best_value = register's "R049/2006-NL1-2013.01 Rev. 3".

Also could the Rev. 3 vs "revision 3" be considered? Same revision, same-entity. The document also says "revision 3" spelled out; that's just formatting.
